reason: The text explicitly demonstrates the Hebrews/Israelites as followers of Yahweh through multiple indicators: (1) when facing the Egyptian army, the people's immediate response is to cry out to Yahweh (וַיִּצְעֲק֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה); (2) Moses exhorts them to trust in 'the salvation of Yahweh' and directs them to stand firm as Yahweh fights for them; (3) the narrative explicitly resolves by stating 'the people feared the Lord and believed in the Lord' (וַיִּֽירְא֥וּ הָעָ֖ם אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּֽאֲמִ֙ינוּ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה). The passage portrays the Hebrews' primary identity and recourse as devotion to and reliance upon Yahweh, not military strength or other means.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
